recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-16027 unless a new work-group issue reopens the broader AdverseEvent clinical-research date model.
issue_request: Published Patient Care change request, Persuasive with Modification, asking AdverseEvent to add a dateTime 0..1 detected element for when the adverse event was detected and a dateTime 0..1 first-recorded element, originally described as assertedDate, while distinguishing these from the existing occurrence date.
initial_application: Historical commit 722ed5c93f4bc9828e96f0f5b476bedc3486fb92 explicitly references GF#16027 and added AdverseEvent.detected plus AdverseEvent.recordedDate to the AdverseEvent spreadsheet source. The current StructureDefinition carries the same semantics after later source refactors.
additional_context: FHIR-17285 records the broader Patient Care recordedDate versus assertedDate distinction that explains the current recordedDate name and comment. FHIR-22737 later addressed AdverseEvent element ordering while preserving detected and recordedDate. FHIR-24684 later rejected renaming detected to assertedDate. Zulip and Confluence searches found no direct contrary FHIR-16027 decision; broader Patient Care minutes discuss later AdverseEvent date-model questions without invalidating these elements.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. source/fhir.ini keeps AdverseEvent in the active build, and source/adverseevent/structuredefinition-AdverseEvent.xml already defines AdverseEvent.detected as 0..1 dateTime with the requested reporter-opinion definition and AdverseEvent.recordedDate as 0..1 dateTime with the first-recorded definition/comment and GF#16027/GF#17285 committee note.
